title: Operational playbook: reshard dedicated pools & automatic fallback after scaling regression
creator: Priya Nair
description: Create and validate an operational playbook for rapid resharding of dedicated GPU pools and an automatic fallback path when autoscaling regressions cause capacity shortfalls. This ticket codifies detection thresholds, temporary evacuation/reshard steps, throttling rules, communication templates, and durable post-incident mitigations so on-call and SRE can restore throughput quickly while avoiding cascading SLA breaches.

incident_impact: High — Several mid-market and enterprise Dedicated customers experienced degraded throughput and increased tail latency for ~2 hours. SLA credit window triggered for two contracts. No data loss, but customer-facing features experienced timeouts and degraded UX.
rca_summary: A recently rolled kernel-safety throttling change in the autoscaler increased decision latency under certain GC patterns and long sequence-length requests. That caused the autoscaler to under-react to load, leaving pools below committed throughput. The lack of a tested automated resharding/evacuation path and conservative throttles on service-to-service spillover prevented rapid redistribution of headroom. Contributing factors: insufficient canary coverage for bursty request shapes, and missing observability mapping between autoscaler decisions and pool-level headroom metrics.
mitigation_during_incident: Enable soft-evacuation routing to move new traffic to standby pools in another region
Manual resharding: reclamation of two underused reservations and reassign to impacted dedicated pool
Temporarily relax throttle on cross-pool spillover to allow emergency routing of non-SLA-critical requests
Increase autoscaler decision frequency while temporarily reducing conservative damping parameters
Communicate to affected customers via status page and targeted outbound messages; offer postmortem and credit follow-up
long_term_action_items: 1) Implement automated reshard controller: detect headroom deficit and run a safe reshard plan (validate node availability, live-evacuation threshold, pacing) - owner: Liam
2) Add an emergency fallback model variant registry that can be atomically swapped to lower-cost/quantized variants for burst headroom relief - owner: Priya
3) Patch autoscaler rollout gating to include bursty-request canaries and sequence-length synthetic tests - owner: SRE team lead
4) Enrich telemetry: emit per-pool headroom, spillover_count, and last_successful_scale_to to make RCA and alerting more actionable - owner: Observability
5) Create the Dedicated Reshard Runbook (playbook doc) with decision trees, command shortcuts, and communication templates - owner: Liam
6) Implement automated throttling policies that preserve committed throughput (SLA-protect lanes) and allow best-effort spillover for non-SLA traffic - owner: Runtime team
7) Add end-to-end smoke tests in CI that simulate the slow-autoscaler scenario and verify automatic fallback engages - owner: QA
8) Schedule a 90-day verification window after changes to monitor for regression and validate metrics - owner: Program Manager
